neighbours.label: oral, epic or sung transmission of texts (oral poetry, Homeric epics, composed by bards), the other side of a spoken/written distinction whose written side ('committed to writing') is the - pole
fire: For centuries the poems were passed down in the form of oral poetry.
The Homeric epics were sung by bards long before anyone wrote them down.
Homer was a blind poet who recited his verses from memory.
The Vedas were composed by priests and kept alive through chanting.
Storytellers in the village memorized long ballads of their ancestors.
Scholars study the oral formulas that helped singers remember the epic.
The saga was recited aloud at feasts for generations.
Griots in West Africa preserve family histories through song.
quiet: For centuries the poems were copied by monks onto parchment.
The Homeric epics were printed in Venice in a fine edition.
Homer's translator worked at a desk with a pen and notebook.
The Vedas were edited by scholars and published in many volumes.
Clerks in the village recorded the land deeds of their ancestors.
Scholars study the handwriting that helped date the manuscript.
The saga was written on vellum and stored in a monastery.
Archives in West Africa preserve family histories in letters.

notes: logit effect suppresses ' write'/' writing'/' written'; the - pole fires where 'writing' is the expected next word
